status: Proposal only — no Figma or application edits made during this audit
method: Live top-level inventory and all visible text captured from all 1,055 nodes on Pages 24–29, static source/route/contract walkthrough, and targeted rendered review of six high-risk candidates plus screenshots inspected earlier in the session. This is not a fresh pixel-by-pixel review of every screen, runtime test, provider qualification, or proof of feature completion. Current dirty working tree was read as-is.
decisionHierarchy: Direct user corrections > current product direction > older detailed presentation contracts. Current code is evidence of implementation, not authority to resurrect rejected UI.

direction.note: Images, clips and finished videos; no required creation order. Latest review decisions override older presentation choices.

rejections.note: October 13 rejected titles, drafts UI, repair notices, comparison banners and dialogs.

free.note: Free testing; no customer credits, checkout or paid Keep contract.

routes.note: Actual mounted routes: /app and /app/project plus retained workspace, auth, docs, account, Sketch, Studio and sharing. New public-page modules are not mounted here.

workspace.note: Current workspace still has obsolete headers/drafts UI; history/media are present, editor/export are not activated.

drafts.note: Draft revision/conflict retention exists. It does not require the rejected draft-manager or merge dialog.

composer.note: Current code still offers Highlights toggle, Review request then Generate, and routine save labels; these conflict with review decisions.

phrase.note: Exact phrase binding/application exists. Loading, stale, repeated-phrase and failure cases belong to the same composer interaction.

viewer.note: Media viewing, video playback, access retry, Details, reuse and input selection exist. Code still splits playback and actions.

history.note: History renders accepted requests, output slots and their media; outcomes belong to their original request.

profiles.note: Default new-workflow profiles are unqualified. Wan video profiles have maxCount 1; Wan 2.5 has only a start-frame role; image editing has a primary image, no mask role.

admission.note: Blocks unqualified profiles, incompatible input roles, unsupported values and counts; this is validation, not a reason for separate full-screen steps.

context.note: Exact branch/project instructions are materialized. This does not implement the proposed summary/directions-selection UI.

planned.note: Video editing/export are explicitly proposed. Do not delete this agreed feature merely because production implementation is incomplete.

oldcontract.note: Older detailed contract specifies context/draft/recovery behaviors; several presentation choices were superseded in this conversation. Simplifying additional gates is a proposal, not an already approved contract change.

editor.note: Current UI explicitly says editing/export are not activated; searched source tree has no composition-renderer/editor implementation.

deferred.note: Dedicated image editor is deferred; normal image generation and prompt-based editing remain in scope.

auth.note: Authentication, verification and password-reset routes exist. Preserve their error handling when consolidating design frames.

account.note: Current account has actual identity, verification/reset and sign-out behavior; proposed account extensions are not all implemented.

support.note: Support uses mailto. It does not prove a mail app opened, a message was sent or a support ticket was created.

public.note: Proposed landing/product/pricing module exists, but App.tsx does not mount it; route gap is not proof the proposed product pages are invalid.

veo.note: Existing provider adapter has end-image, references and extension paths; native extension is not an invented feature, although the new workspace profile is not qualified.

recraft.note: Recraft models exist in Studio. Do not call them nonexistent merely because the new workflow catalog does not expose them.

utilities.note: Background removal and vectorization are real Studio utility operations; the new workspace needs capability/action integration, not blanket deletion.

toolbar.note: Current shared toolbar family is 1379:84830; centered instances were verified. Nested transport and menu sources are dependencies, not replacement masters.

proposed.note: Account, native handoffs, docs and responsive behavior are part of the proposed full-product scope; state coverage is not a demand for a separate app route per state.

findings.title: Rejected concepts survive under different wording and in shared masters
findings.detail: C11/C29/B05 still present draft comparisons; W22 still says Repairing; Save indicator, Draft comparison, Connection status, Sheet and Conversation menu preserve rejected controls. H07/N58 still teach copy comparison. Earlier literal-text cleanup was incomplete.

findings.title: Separate state machines were turned into separate screens
findings.detail: Queued/running/ready, stale acknowledgements, capability refresh, audio-stream checks, download-started and background completion are largely variants or tests. Keep a compact request/history or field state, not a parallel navigation step.

findings.title: Paid and free flows contradict each other
findings.detail: D09/D10/D12–D14 advertise actual credits, estimates, settlement and checkout while the project is free. K21/N26 invent a Billing destination whose only content says billing is unavailable; K15/N109 show zero-credit receipts.

findings.title: Deferred image canvas is promoted as ready; real utilities need separate treatment
findings.detail: M10–M12/B06 and H20/N65 expose masking/region editing that was deferred. Remove active docs/nav links too. Background removal and vectorization are real Studio operations: C34 and Image tools need integration/availability correction, not deletion as nonexistent features. Keep ordinary image generation, prompt-based edits and Sketch.

findings.title: Page 27 should be a capability reference, not 57 more workflow screens
findings.detail: Its 35 G, 10 R and 12 E scenes duplicate composer/viewer/editor surfaces. Move valid model rules into components and tests. G13/G14/G15 advertise an audio input not exposed by the current Wan workflow profile.

findings.title: Video-batch examples have no matching current profile
findings.detail: W13/W41/W42/W44/W45 show multiple video slots. The exposed video profiles have maxCount 1; image profiles can support a multi-output fixture. Rework the example instead of dropping stable slot semantics.

findings.title: Draft/context administration adds unnecessary decisions
findings.detail: C18/C19/C27 make the creator manage branch instructions, summaries and instruction versions. Propose removing these dedicated approval gates. This revises older proposed interactions; it is not a claim that their underlying context data does not exist.

findings.title: Retry is burdened with another confirmation screen
findings.detail: W18/W43 add a new review after an explicit retry choice. Propose a single retry action with exact original input retention and a new request identity; preserve cancellation and ownership rules.

findings.title: Different generations of workspace navigation coexist
findings.detail: Page 25 rail/project-media shells, Page 27 Source navigation with Image/Video divisions, and Page 28 ongoing conversation workspace compete. Use one shell with intentional sidebar modes. Keep the expanded sidebar master 1029:84401; retire the older Source navigation only after consumers move.

findings.title: The image toolbar contains disabled video controls
findings.detail: The Image transport variant currently includes play, seek and volume solely to fill the full toolbar. Keep one reusable full-toolbar family with meaningful image actions; do not force video semantics onto a still image or create another floating mini-toolbar.

findings.title: Account/docs/support are over-expanded into snapshot catalogs
findings.detail: Keep actual sign-in, signup, verification, reset, account, documentation and contact surfaces. Consolidate error/success/mobile/FAQ copies into reusable states; preserve native errors and accessibility behavior. Billing and region-editor pages are separate removals, not generic consolidation.

findings.title: Current code is not fully consistent with the approved redesign
findings.detail: ProjectWorkspace still renders Drafts and redundant headers; PromptComposer has a Highlights toggle, stale Review current phrase, Review request then Generate, and routine save labels. MediaViewer still has a title and two action rows. These are code follow-ups, not reasons to restore rejected designs.

findings.title: Proposed public pages are not routed yet
findings.detail: PublicPages.tsx contains landing/product/pricing views, but App.tsx still mounts the retained workspace at / and lacks these new public routes. Keep agreed public-page design intent; label implementation gaps and fix broken future links during implementation.

findings.title: Prototype scaffolding must not be mistaken for product navigation
findings.detail: Applied/Return clones and Oxx/menu/Output settings overlay frames are often reaction destinations. Archive duplicates only after rewiring; do not delete nested toolbar sources or leave broken links.

findings.title: Implementation gaps do not invalidate accepted features
findings.detail: Keep video assembly, trim, captions, audio, export, public sharing, history and Sketch within the agreed scope. Veo extension exists in the retained provider; Recraft, background removal and vectorization exist in Studio. Distinguish retained code from new-workspace qualification and complete end-to-end behavior.

findings.title: Empty shells are still indexed as completed scenario evidence
findings.detail: R06/R07/R09/R10/E11 on Page 27 and W28/W21 on Page 28 still occupy canvas space after their defining UI was removed. Remove obsolete index/acceptance references as part of an approved cleanup; do not claim those frames still demonstrate the removed feature.

This Privacy Policy explains how Vidra
(“we”, “us”, “our”)
collects, uses, and shares information when you use
Vidra (the “Service”).
Questions? Contact us at support@vidra.app
.

• Account information: email, display name, auth identifiers.
• Content you submit: prompts, outputs, saved assets. Shared content may be accessible via link.
• Usage and device info: interactions, pages viewed, diagnostic logs, performance metrics.

AI processing.
When you use AI features, we send inputs to the relevant AI
provider to process your request and return results.

• Provide, maintain, and improve the Service.
• Authenticate you and secure accounts.
• Process payments and prevent fraud.
• Debug issues and measure performance.
• Communicate about updates and support requests.

providers you use through the Service. We may share to comply with law, protect rights/safety, or in connection with a business transfer. We do not sell personal information.
We retain information as needed to provide the Service and for legitimate business purposes. You can request deletion, subject to legal and operational requirements.

• Access and update account information in the Service.
• Request deletion of your account and saved content.
• Opt out of non-essential communications.
• EEA/UK residents may have additional rights (access, correction, portability, objection, restriction).
We use administrative, technical, and physical safeguards. No method is 100% secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security.
We and our service providers may process information in other countries. We take steps to protect it as required by applicable law.

This Privacy Policy explains how Vidra
(“we”, “us”, “our”)
collects, uses, and shares information when you use
Vidra (the “Service”).
Questions? Contact us at support@vidra.app
.

• Account information: email, display name, auth identifiers.
• Content you submit: prompts, outputs, saved assets. Shared content may be accessible via link.
• Usage and device info: interactions, pages viewed, diagnostic logs, performance metrics.
• Billing information: processed by Stripe. We receive limited metadata; never full card numbers.

AI processing.
When you use AI features, we send inputs to the relevant AI
provider to process your request and return results.

• Provide, maintain, and improve the Service.
• Authenticate you and secure accounts.
• Process payments and prevent fraud.
• Debug issues and measure performance.
